messages:
Samir Rao: Heads-up: ran rk-v2-ptq on the "sparse-short" locked holdout. NDCG@10 down 3.2% vs rk-v1-prod. Distribution looks concentrated on exact-match short queries.
Nina Park: Is this the new per-channel quant calibration or default PTQ?
Samir Rao: Default PTQ (no per-channel clipping) using our compress pipeline. Command:
```
./run_eval --model rk-v2-ptq --holdout holdouts/sparse-short.csv --metrics ndcg@10,mrr,recall@5 --seed 1337 --batch 128 --kvpack true
```
Toby Li: Do you have the per-query delta histogram? Could be a handful of anchor queries with high impact.
Samir Rao: Uploaded the histogram gist. Peak at -0.9 per-query delta for ~120 queries. Median delta is -0.02.
Rhea Singh: That pattern smells like a calibration shift rather than systemic rank swap. Try temperature scaling on logits before score -> rank. E.g., divide logits by 0.95 or 1.1.
Samir Rao: Tried T=0.9,1.0,1.1. Best was T=0.92 which recovered ~1.8% but still -1.4% net.
Nina Park: Could quantization be affecting attention scoring on short contexts? Int8 can bias heads with small magnitude weights. Can you run per-layer max-abs to see which layers lose dynamic range?
Samir Rao: Per-layer max diffs: layers 1-3 show bigger abs shrink (~6-9%) vs tail layers.
Toby Li: Then try layerwise quant scale re-estimation (per-channel), or keep first few layers in fp16. Quick test: fp16-first3 + rest-int8.
Samir Rao: Running fp16-first3 iteration now.
CI Bot: Job queued: eval-rerank-3494000000-fp16first3 (id: job-8821).
Rhea Singh: Also check candidate framing: short queries sometimes produce passage candidates vs doc candidates; scoring pref differs if doc length bias exists. Please run eval with doc_normalize flag toggled.
Samir Rao: Ran doc_normalize true/false. With normalization on, rk-v2-ptq loses less (delta -1.0%). Without normalize it's -2.9%. So normalization helps.
Nina Park: Interesting. Could be that quantized model undervalues exact token overlap signals which doc_normalize boosts.
Toby Li: For model onboarding policy: propose adding a "sparse-short" gate in CI that requires NDCG within 1% of prod or a documented mitigation (temp scaling, fp16-firstN, or feature signal).
Rhea Singh: Agree. Also add an automated priming probe: prepend a [KW] token to short queries and measure delta; if priming recovers >1% that indicates a mismatched scoring preference rather than data leakage.
Samir Rao: Priming probe results: [KW] prefix improved NDCG by +2.1 vs unprimed q for rk-v2-ptq. fp16-first3 recovered +2.4 vs plain ptq.
Nina Park: Sounds like a viable mitigation path. Which is cheaper? Priming is free at eval, but it requires downstream infra to add token prefix at serving. fp16-first3 ups GPU memory cost.
Toby Li: We should quantify latency/cost tradeoff before deciding. Add a smoke bench for latency and memory for fp16-first3 vs priming.
CI Bot: New smoke job scheduled: rerank-memlat-bench (models: rk-v1-prod, rk-v2-ptq, rk-v2-ptq-fp16first3) (id: job-8825).
Rhea Singh: Also validate that the eval harness uses identical gain function (prod uses exponential gain by default?) Double-check --gain linear vs exponential.
Samir Rao: Confirmed harness set to linear gains and cutoff 10. No mismatch.
Nina Park: OK next steps: 1) Wait for fp16-first3 eval/bench; 2) add sparse-short gate to CI; 3) prototype priming prefix in lightweight feature server and run A/B in canary. I'll draft the CI PR.
Samir Rao: I'll paste results when bench completes. Thanks all. :rocket:
